She covers method choices from assertions and semantic similarity to auxiliary ML models and LLM as a judge, including regression testing and the trade offs of each approach.

nodes.label: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing in MLOps
nodes.title: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing in MLOps
nodes.search: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing in MLOps A practical guide to A/B testing models in an MLOps context: routing user traffic between model versions A and B on Kubernetes with Seldon and Prometheus, and comparing their performance through Grafana dashboards and a Streamlit based traffic simulation.

nodes.label: Active and Self-Supervised Learning for Data Selection
nodes.title: Active and Self-Supervised Learning for Data Selection
nodes.search: Active and Self Supervised Learning for Data Selection How active learning and self supervised contrastive approaches change data selection for deep learning on unstructured data such as images, audio, and text.

nodes.label: AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp 2025 Course Launch
nodes.title: AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp 2025 Course Launch
nodes.search: AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp 2025 Course Launch Launch of the first AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp, a free course teaching developers to use AI tools like Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Codex, and Claude Code, with modules covering the AI tool landscape, an end to end full stack project, agents and MCP, building your own coding agent, DevOps and CI/CD, and automation.

nodes.label: AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp 2025 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.title: AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp 2025 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.search: AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp 2025 Pre Course Live Q&A Pre course live Q&A for AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp 2025: Alexey clarifies the course scope — developer productivity with tools like Cursor, Copilot, and Claude Code rather than AI engineering — explains which Copilot modes (agent, edit, ask) he uses for coding, and points people wanting RAG and LangGraph content to LLM Zoomcamp instead.

nodes.label: AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp 2026 Course Launch
nodes.title: AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp 2026 Course Launch
nodes.search: AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp 2026 Course Launch Launch session for the second edition of AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp, a roughly seven week course (four modules plus a project period) on AI native development: choosing a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot), spec driven development, building and deploying end to end applications, with materials hosted on Substack and the instructor's own AI built tools (a serverless AWS Lambda Q&A app replacing a paid Slido subscription) as examples.

nodes.label: AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp 2026 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.title: AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp 2026 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.search: AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp 2026 Pre Course Live Q&A Pre course Q&A for AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp 2026: the five week spec driven development path from building an app with AI coding assistants to deploying it and making it production ready, why MCP and building coding agents were dropped from the curriculum now that agents handle those tasks, running local LLMs for coding being too slow without a GPU, and project requirements such as a database, containers, integration tests, and cloud deployment.

nodes.label: AI in Fashion - Size & Fit
nodes.title: AI in Fashion - Size & Fit
nodes.search: AI in Fashion Size & Fit A Zalando applied scientist explains the size and fit problem, where roughly half of online fashion purchases are returned and about a third for size reasons, and describes production size recommendation algorithms, including a meta learning deep recommender that learns customer, article, and size embeddings from purchase history and questionnaire data; also discusses why GAN based virtual try on fails to capture real fit and why garment blueprint data is hard to obtain.

nodes.label: AI Math Olympiad: A Technical Debrief of the Competition
nodes.title: AI Math Olympiad: A Technical Debrief of the Competition
nodes.search: AI Math Olympiad: A Technical Debrief of the Competition Technical debrief of the AI Mathematical Olympiad (AIMO) Kaggle competition by a silver medalist, covering the problem setup, how LLMs are trained for math reasoning, and competition baselines. It explains winning techniques such as quantization with AutoAWQ and NVIDIA's OpenMathReasoning dataset with Qwen 2.5 fine tuning and genSelect candidate selection, plus caveats about LLM output variance and competition evaluation.

nodes.label: AI-Powered Computer Vision Applications in Media Industry
nodes.title: AI-Powered Computer Vision Applications in Media Industry
nodes.search: AI Powered Computer Vision Applications in Media Industry Webinar, on 2021 12 07, with Yulia Pavlova.

nodes.label: Algorithmic Fairness
nodes.title: Algorithmic Fairness
nodes.search: Algorithmic Fairness An overview of algorithmic fairness covering where bias enters models (with hiring algorithms like Amazon's as examples), the landscape of fairness toolkits including Google's What If Tool, Microsoft's Fairlearn, and AWS SageMaker Clarify, and methods such as fairness metrics, threshold adjustment, and causal reasoning.

nodes.label: Analytics Engineering with dbt Workshop
nodes.title: Analytics Engineering with dbt Workshop
nodes.search: Analytics Engineering with dbt Workshop dbt workshop led by Juan, co author of Fundamentals of Analytics Engineering: framing dbt as data transformation with software engineering best practices, then building and debugging dbt models for NYC taxi data in BigQuery, including fixing mismatched column names and running dbt run.

nodes.label: Analytics Use Cases Across Non-Automated Operations
nodes.title: Analytics Use Cases Across Non-Automated Operations
nodes.search: Analytics Use Cases Across Non Automated Operations The associate director of data at HelloFresh Canada shows how analytics and machine learning create value in physical, non automated operations such as meal kit manufacturing, inventory, and supplier optimization, and discusses the challenges of fragmented systems, manual data collection, and poor metric definitions in these environments.

nodes.label: Applied Causal Inference
nodes.title: Applied Causal Inference
nodes.search: Applied Causal Inference Webinar, on 2024 01 28, with Irina Brudaru.

nodes.label: Automated Prompt Optimization with Evidently AI
nodes.title: Automated Prompt Optimization with Evidently AI
nodes.search: Automated Prompt Optimization with Evidently AI Evidently AI webinar on automated prompt optimization: Mikhail shows the implementation that takes an evaluation dataset, the current prompt, and logged mistake rows, then asks an LLM to rewrite the prompt — with the key trick of instructing it to generalize from failure examples so quality improves without overfitting to specific rows.

nodes.label: AWS Glue DataBrew
nodes.title: AWS Glue DataBrew
nodes.search: AWS Glue DataBrew Live coding tour of AWS Glue DataBrew shortly after launch, using the New York Airbnb open dataset to show how data scientists and analysts can prepare data without writing code.

nodes.label: Back-of-the-Envelope Calculation For Machine Learning Projects
nodes.title: Back-of-the-Envelope Calculation For Machine Learning Projects
nodes.search: Back of the Envelope Calculation For Machine Learning Projects A data science practitioner shows how to plan machine learning projects with the ML Canvas, using back of the envelope calculations to reason about business value and KPIs, the prediction versus training sides of the canvas, and feasibility before committing to yet another proof of concept.

nodes.label: Best MLOps Practices for Building End-to-End ML Projects
nodes.title: Best MLOps Practices for Building End-to-End ML Projects
nodes.search: Best MLOps Practices for Building End to End ML Projects Workshop applying MLOps best practices to an end to end computer vision project with DVC: data versioning, machine learning pipelines, experiment management, and leveraging CI/CD practices and cloud resources for reproducible deep learning training.

nodes.label: Bodywork: GitOps for Machine Learning
nodes.title: Bodywork: GitOps for Machine Learning
nodes.search: Bodywork: GitOps for Machine Learning Bodywork's co founder shows how GitOps automation deploys machine learning projects to production continuously, why deployment is hard for data teams, and case studies of the pattern in operation.

nodes.label: Bring Your Own Data
nodes.title: Bring Your Own Data
nodes.search: Bring Your Own Data Workshop on collecting your own dataset for the Kaggle kitchenware classification competition: gathering images of cups, glasses, and cutlery with Toloka crowd workers, deduplicating them with Elasticsearch, annotating, and storing the results in AWS S3 for model training.

nodes.label: Build Agentic Assistants with OpenAI Function Calling: Part 2
nodes.title: Build Agentic Assistants with OpenAI Function Calling: Part 2
nodes.search: Build Agentic Assistants with OpenAI Function Calling: Part 2 Part 2 of the agentic assistants workshop, recapping the RAG and agentic search assistant from part 1 and deep diving into the OpenAI function calling loop that lets the model decide when to invoke tools such as search over course FAQ documents. Alexey Grigorev refactors the code into reusable classes and his toy ai kit library with a swappable chat interface.

nodes.label: Build an AI Coding Agent
nodes.title: Build an AI Coding Agent
nodes.search: Build an AI Coding Agent Workshop building a coding agent from scratch that scaffolds a Django to do application: implementing file read/write, file tree, grep, and bash execution tools exposed to the model via OpenAI function calling, with tool schemas auto generated from docstrings in the toy ai kit library. Part of the upcoming AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp, it also tests behavior with GPT 4o mini versus GPT 5 and references tools like Lovable and Cursor.

nodes.label: Build an LLM Wiki for Agent Long-Term Memory
nodes.title: Build an LLM Wiki for Agent Long-Term Memory
nodes.search: Build an LLM Wiki for Agent Long Term Memory Workshop, on 2026 09 08, with Paul Iusztin.

nodes.label: Build and Ship an AI-Assisted Full-Stack App
nodes.title: Build and Ship an AI-Assisted Full-Stack App
nodes.search: Build and Ship an AI Assisted Full Stack App Second live coding session of AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp that builds a full stack system design interview app with AI coding agents: a frontend plus an OpenAPI specification, a FastAPI backend with SQLite, and packaging of frontend and backend in Docker so the app can be deployed anywhere.

nodes.label: Build Your AI Machine Vision System by Yourself
nodes.title: Build Your AI Machine Vision System by Yourself
nodes.search: Build Your AI Machine Vision System by Yourself How to build a complete industrial machine vision system, from camera and lighting hardware choices including infrared for reflective sheets to classic or AI based inspection code that replaces costly human inspection.

nodes.label: Build Your First RAG Application with LLMs
nodes.title: Build Your First RAG Application with LLMs
nodes.search: Build Your First RAG Application with LLMs First workshop in the LLM Zoomcamp 2026 series: building a basic RAG application over the DataTalks.Club FAQ dataset with text search, the OpenAI API, and prompt assembly, including computing request cost from input, cached, and output token counts against GPT 5 Mini pricing.

nodes.label: Building a Group Wide Data Lakehouse for Data Science & BI
nodes.title: Building a Group Wide Data Lakehouse for Data Science & BI
nodes.search: Building a Group Wide Data Lakehouse for Data Science & BI A lead data architect at MyLight explains building a group wide Databricks lakehouse with a bronze/silver/gold medallion architecture, starting from a pilot and migrating off the legacy stack while monitoring platform and cloud costs, logging via a custom Python plus Azure telemetry logger, and serving both data scientists (notebooks, Databricks SQL workspace) and business reporting in Power BI.

nodes.label: Building AI Agent Workflows with Switch
nodes.title: Building AI Agent Workflows with Switch
nodes.search: Building AI Agent Workflows with Switch Workshop, on 2026 09 15, with Louis Amaudruz.

nodes.label: Building an AI Stock Research Agent
nodes.title: Building an AI Stock Research Agent
nodes.search: Building an AI Stock Research Agent Stock Markets Analytics Zoomcamp instructor Ivan builds an AI stock research agent live: it pulls company fundamentals and news from Yahoo Finance and social posts from X and Reddit via the xAI API using the OpenAI compatible client, then feeds that data to an LLM to analyze companies, with the explicit caveat that the output is not investment advice.

nodes.label: Building an ML Service Platform from the Ground Up
nodes.title: Building an ML Service Platform from the Ground Up
nodes.search: Building an ML Service Platform from the Ground Up Why deploying and serving ML models is harder than traditional services due to added model and data complexity, and how BentoML, an open source ML service platform, packages models and runs them as production services on Kubernetes.

nodes.label: Building an ML System for Southeast Asia’s Largest Hospital Group
nodes.title: Building an ML System for Southeast Asia’s Largest Hospital Group
nodes.search: Building an ML System for Southeast Asia’s Largest Hospital Group Building an ML system for a large Southeast Asia hospital group to give patients accurate upfront treatment cost estimates, improving patient experience and reducing unpaid procedures.

nodes.label: Building an Open-Source Feature Store with Apache Flink
nodes.title: Building an Open-Source Feature Store with Apache Flink
nodes.search: Building an Open Source Feature Store with Apache Flink A Findifi engineer explains the ranking and relevancy problems that pushed the e commerce search company toward the feature store approach, and how they built an open source feature store on Apache Flink to compute features for search, recommendations, and personalization.

nodes.label: Building and Scaling a Machine Learning Platform
nodes.title: Building and Scaling a Machine Learning Platform
nodes.search: Building and Scaling a Machine Learning Platform How BMW in Munich justified, built, and scaled its internal Connected AI machine learning platform: the platform's features and architecture for connected vehicle use cases, and learnings from onboarding a diverse range of data scientists onto reusable tooling.

nodes.label: Building Data-Intensive Teams
nodes.title: Building Data-Intensive Teams
nodes.search: Building Data Intensive Teams What makes a team data intensive, drawing on Kleppmann's definition of data intensive applications and the experience of running data products at scale.

nodes.label: Building Machine Learning Pipelines with Kedro
nodes.title: Building Machine Learning Pipelines with Kedro
nodes.search: Building Machine Learning Pipelines with Kedro Merel Thijssen, a QuantumBlack engineer working on Kedro, introduces the open source framework for building reproducible, modular machine learning pipelines, explains how it fits a data science workflow, and codes through an example pipeline live.

nodes.label: Building Scalable End-to-End Deep Learning Pipelines in the Cloud
nodes.title: Building Scalable End-to-End Deep Learning Pipelines in the Cloud
nodes.search: Building Scalable End to End Deep Learning Pipelines in the Cloud Building scalable deep learning pipelines in the cloud with cloud native orchestrators: organizing multi service pipelines, keeping model work iterative, and integrating with existing infrastructure.

nodes.label: Building Streaming Analytics: The Journey and Learnings
nodes.title: Building Streaming Analytics: The Journey and Learnings
nodes.search: Building Streaming Analytics: The Journey and Learnings A serial data platform founder and CTO shares lessons from two decades of building streaming analytics, from early days Kafka, Spark, and Cassandra stacks through lambda and kappa architectures, with practical guidance on when to use which.

nodes.label: Building the End to end Roadmap for your Data
nodes.title: Building the End to end Roadmap for your Data
nodes.search: Building the End to end Roadmap for your Data An end to end roadmap for organizational data presented from a health law and risk management perspective: privacy obligations, data governance, and risk impact when building data repositories across sectors like healthcare.

nodes.label: Building the Modern Geospatial Data Stack
nodes.title: Building the Modern Geospatial Data Stack
nodes.search: Building the Modern Geospatial Data Stack How Planet, the daily satellite imaging company, builds its geospatial data stack: the satellite tasking system, working with STAC catalogs and BigQuery in the cloud, and the challenges of transforming raw imagery into usable geospatial metrics.

nodes.label: Building with MCP: Tools, Workflows, and Real Examples
nodes.title: Building with MCP: Tools, Workflows, and Real Examples
nodes.search: Building with MCP: Tools, Workflows, and Real Examples MCP workshop with Bhavani Ravi covering the fundamentals of Model Context Protocol — servers, clients, and stdio versus streamable HTTP transports — followed by real examples of plugging MCP servers into GitHub Copilot and other AI coding assistants to give agents access to external tools in everyday dev workflows.

nodes.label: Career Transitioning into Data Science
nodes.title: Career Transitioning into Data Science
nodes.search: Career Transitioning into Data Science An electrical engineer turned data scientist shares her transition story, including a three year career break, Kaggle notebooks as a learning path, and mentoring women in data science.

nodes.label: Chat with Your Own Data: Introduction to the LLM Zoomcamp
nodes.title: Chat with Your Own Data: Introduction to the LLM Zoomcamp
nodes.search: Chat with Your Own Data: Introduction to the LLM Zoomcamp Pre course workshop introducing LLM Zoomcamp by building a question answering RAG system over the DataTalks.Club course FAQ documents: indexing Q&A records in Elasticsearch with field boosting and course filters, retrieving the top matches, and prompting OpenAI GPT 3.5 to generate answers. It also outlines the course syllabus and discusses hallucination risks and self hosting Elasticsearch for sensitive data.

nodes.label: Combining Quantum and AI for Accelerating CFD Simulations - Part 1
nodes.title: Combining Quantum and AI for Accelerating CFD Simulations - Part 1
nodes.search: Combining Quantum and AI for Accelerating CFD Simulations Part 1 Part 1 of a Quasi startup workshop on accelerating CFD simulations by combining physics based machine learning with quantum computing: Adi and Bayang explain the motivation and use cases, and walk through neural architectures with spatial temporal encoders and weight balancing terms they are rebuilding from papers for crystal growth simulation.

nodes.label: Context Engineering for Agentic Hybrid Applications
nodes.title: Context Engineering for Agentic Hybrid Applications
nodes.search: Context Engineering for Agentic Hybrid Applications Two part webinar on context engineering for agentic applications: Tobias (JetBrains) presents research on making coding agents more efficient and reliable by summarizing and masking the ReAct trajectory's tool outputs, and Ivan covers practical techniques including guardrails around tool calls, prefix/KV caching, and trimming verbose observations to keep only useful information.

nodes.label: Continuous Integration for Machine Learning
nodes.title: Continuous Integration for Machine Learning
nodes.search: Continuous Integration for Machine Learning Continuous integration for machine learning from an Iterative/DVC engineer: applying version control and CI practices to data, models, and code at the data science and DevOps intersection.

nodes.label: Conversational AI
nodes.title: Conversational AI
nodes.search: Conversational AI An introduction to conversational AI that breaks down how non end to end dialogue systems work: intent recognition, entity and named entity extraction with slot filling, dialogue management combining AI and rule based systems, and question answering over knowledge bases.

nodes.label: Customer Segmentation 2.0
nodes.title: Customer Segmentation 2.0
nodes.search: Customer Segmentation 2.0 A customer segmentation walk through, from exploring the raw data to the segmentation approach, based on a real hiring process assignment and US healthcare analytics experience.

nodes.label: Dangers of Dirty Data
nodes.title: Dangers of Dirty Data
nodes.search: Dangers of Dirty Data What dirty data looks like inside organizations, why data quality matters, the consequences of leaving it untidy, and simple spot checking practices for data accuracy.

nodes.label: Data Engineering Zoomcamp 2026 Course Launch
nodes.title: Data Engineering Zoomcamp 2026 Course Launch
nodes.search: Data Engineering Zoomcamp 2026 Course Launch Launch of the fifth Data Engineering Zoomcamp cohort: Alexey outlines the six modules (Docker and Terraform, Kestra orchestration, BigQuery warehousing, dbt analytics engineering, Spark batch, and streaming), introduces the course team and logistics, and spends most of the session answering community questions.

nodes.label: Data Engineering Zoomcamp 2026 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.title: Data Engineering Zoomcamp 2026 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.search: Data Engineering Zoomcamp 2026 Pre Course Live Q&A Pre course live Q&A for Data Engineering Zoomcamp 2026 covering the biggest update in five years of the syllabus (Docker, Terraform, Kestra, BigQuery, dbt, Spark, streaming), prerequisites, and candid career questions such as the odds of landing a data engineering job without prior experience and how AI coding tools change the hiring picture.

nodes.label: Data Incident Management with Soda and dbt
nodes.title: Data Incident Management with Soda and dbt
nodes.search: Data Incident Management with Soda and dbt Workshop on data incident management with Soda and dbt: Soda Core's data validation checks and automated monitoring alongside dbt tests, and the workflow for finding, analyzing, and resolving data quality incidents.

nodes.label: Data Ingestion From APIs to Warehouses
nodes.title: Data Ingestion From APIs to Warehouses
nodes.search: Data Ingestion From APIs to Warehouses A hands on DataTalksClub workshop by the creator of dlt (data load tool) on scalable data ingestion from APIs and files: extraction patterns, normalization (typing, flattening nested dictionaries into columns, unrolling arrays into child tables), incremental loading, using DuckDB as a local development destination before switching the same dlt pipeline to BigQuery, and how dlt (extract load) complements dbt (transform).

nodes.label: Data Ingestion From APIs to Warehouses and Data Lakes
nodes.title: Data Ingestion From APIs to Warehouses and Data Lakes
nodes.search: Data Ingestion From APIs to Warehouses and Data Lakes Data Engineering Zoomcamp workshop on data ingestion with dlt, taught by Veta from dlt Hub, covering how to build self managing pipelines from APIs into warehouses like BigQuery and into data lakes using a DuckDB destination. It demonstrates automatic schema detection, flattening nested JSON into child tables, type normalization, schema evolution, and incremental loading.

nodes.label: Data Mesh in Practice
nodes.title: Data Mesh in Practice
nodes.search: Data Mesh in Practice A Zalando data engineering manager walks through the data mesh adoption journey: moving beyond the central data lake, common pitfalls, and the practices that help organizations become data driven.

nodes.label: Data Monetization with Machine Learning
nodes.title: Data Monetization with Machine Learning
nodes.search: Data Monetization with Machine Learning How OLX converts the 1.5 billion rows of data its 100 million monthly customers generate into money with machine learning: customer centric value creation, cross functional ecosystems, and concrete monetization examples such as the OLX ads suggestor and real estate products.

nodes.label: Data Plumbing without the poop
nodes.title: Data Plumbing without the poop
nodes.search: Data Plumbing without the poop Hands on Mage workshop building end to end data pipelines: a Singer based data integration pipeline, transformation pipelines in Python, SQL, and dbt, then adding orchestration, charts, data validations, and data quality/observability on top.

nodes.label: Data Quality and Reliability with Soda Core
nodes.title: Data Quality and Reliability with Soda Core
nodes.search: Data Quality and Reliability with Soda Core A hands on workshop by a Soda Core developer showing how to define and run data quality checks with the SodaCL DSL and Soda Core execution engine against a Postgres database, from writing check configurations to executing them in a Docker based Python environment.

nodes.label: Data Science for Social Good
nodes.title: Data Science for Social Good
nodes.search: Data Science for Social Good How to start and run a Data Science for Social Good initiative, matching charity and NGO beneficiaries with community volunteers to deliver small, impactful data projects.

nodes.label: Data Storytelling in Python Altair
nodes.title: Data Storytelling in Python Altair
nodes.search: Data Storytelling in Python Altair Workshop on data storytelling with Python's Altair library, led by a CNR researcher and data journalism adjunct professor, introducing the DIKW pyramid and tailoring stories to general public, professional, and executive audiences. The hands on case study builds a global surface temperature anomaly chart step by step, adding labels, annotations, and formatting to move from data to information to knowledge.

nodes.label: Data Versioning Explained
nodes.title: Data Versioning Explained
nodes.search: Data Versioning Explained Why data lakes need version control: lakeFS brings Git style branching, resilience, and manageability to object storage data lakes for data engineers.

nodes.label: DataTalks.Club Conference: Career in Data
nodes.title: DataTalks.Club Conference: Career in Data
nodes.search: DataTalks.Club Conference: Career in Data Conference day on data careers: talks and candid conversations about moving into and growing a career in data, with speakers from across the community.

nodes.label: DataTalks.Club Conference: ML in Production
nodes.title: DataTalks.Club Conference: ML in Production
nodes.search: DataTalks.Club Conference: ML in Production Conference day on machine learning in production with four talks: foundational ML engineering practices, productionizing data science, and treating data cleaning as a learning problem.

nodes.label: DataTalks.Club Conference: ML Use Cases
nodes.title: DataTalks.Club Conference: ML Use Cases
nodes.search: DataTalks.Club Conference: ML Use Cases Conference day of machine learning use cases, including industrial reinforcement learning applications and other applied ML talks from the community.

nodes.label: DataTalks.Club Conference: Product and Process
nodes.title: DataTalks.Club Conference: Product and Process
nodes.search: DataTalks.Club Conference: Product and Process Conference day on product and process for data organizations, including how OLX organizes search and recommendations as data intensive product teams.

nodes.label: DataTalks.Club Summer 2025 AI Hackathon Launch
nodes.title: DataTalks.Club Summer 2025 AI Hackathon Launch
nodes.search: DataTalks.Club Summer 2025 AI Hackathon Launch Launch stream for the DataTalks.Club Summer 2025 AI Hackathon, where participants spend the summer building LLM powered projects useful for the community, with AWS credits for top teams. Alexey Grigorev reviews submitted project ideas with feedback, explains the loose judging criteria (impact, implementation, communication), and contrasts hackathon projects with the stricter Zoomcamp capstone requirements.

nodes.label: DataTalks.Club Summer Marathon: Career in Data
nodes.title: DataTalks.Club Summer Marathon: Career in Data
nodes.search: DataTalks.Club Summer Marathon: Career in Data Day one of the DataTalks.Club Summer Marathon opens the career in data week with an interview with Santiago, a director of computer vision solutions, about transitioning from software engineering to machine learning, in a two week conference that also covers promotions, data engineering, and ML production.

nodes.label: DataTalks.Club Summer Marathon: Machine Learning in Production
nodes.title: DataTalks.Club Summer Marathon: Machine Learning in Production
nodes.search: DataTalks.Club Summer Marathon: Machine Learning in Production The Summer Marathon session on ML in production: CARIAD's head of AI presents an AI project canvas for setting up AI projects for success, covering idea generation, scoping, guardrails, and success metrics, and discusses evolving it toward an AI product canvas.

nodes.label: Deep Learning Recommender Systems
nodes.title: Deep Learning Recommender Systems
nodes.search: Deep Learning Recommender Systems OLX data scientists take deep learning recommenders from prototype to production: neural item embeddings for similar item suggestions, A/B experiments to prove value, and a highly automated production model.

nodes.label: Deep Learning with PyTorch
nodes.title: Deep Learning with PyTorch
nodes.search: Deep Learning with PyTorch Hands on workshop implementing the ML Zoomcamp clothing image classification model in PyTorch on Google Colab with a T4 GPU, as a PyTorch alternative to the course's TensorFlow/Keras module. It walks through dataset loading, defining the network, training and validation loops with torch.no grad, and contrasts low level PyTorch with high level Keras.

nodes.label: Deploying ML Models with AWS Lambda (Serverless)
nodes.title: Deploying ML Models with AWS Lambda (Serverless)
nodes.search: Deploying ML Models with AWS Lambda (Serverless) ML Zoomcamp workshop on serverless deployment with AWS Lambda: building a Lambda function that serves a scikit learn logistic regression model as a Docker container image published to ECR, and replacing TensorFlow Lite with ONNX Runtime, including converting Keras and PyTorch clothing classifier models to ONNX. It also covers cold starts, warm invocations, timeout and memory settings, and cost comparisons with SageMaker endpoints.

nodes.label: Deploying ML Models with FastAPI and uv
nodes.title: Deploying ML Models with FastAPI and uv
nodes.search: Deploying ML Models with FastAPI and uv ML Zoomcamp module update workshop that serves the churn prediction model with FastAPI instead of Flask, using uv for dependency management, typed request validation, and uvicorn with auto reload. It containerizes the app with a Dockerfile and demonstrates deploying to fly.io as an alternative to AWS Elastic Beanstalk.

nodes.label: Deploying ML Models with Kubernetes
nodes.title: Deploying ML Models with Kubernetes
nodes.search: Deploying ML Models with Kubernetes ML Zoomcamp workshop that packages the ONNX clothing classification model behind FastAPI (dependency managed with uv) into Docker and deploys it to a local Kubernetes cluster created with kind. It covers kubectl, deployments with replicas, services and load balancing, resource requests/limits, and liveness and readiness probes.

nodes.label: Deploying models with AWS Sagemaker
nodes.title: Deploying models with AWS Sagemaker
nodes.search: Deploying models with AWS Sagemaker Deploying machine learning models with AWS SageMaker, from a trained model artifact to a served production endpoint.

nodes.label: Deploying Serverless Machine Learning with AWS
nodes.title: Deploying Serverless Machine Learning with AWS
nodes.search: Deploying Serverless Machine Learning with AWS A hands on workshop on deploying machine learning models serverlessly on AWS: training a model in a container, packaging the service, and the DevOps skills that make data scientist and data engineer collaboration productive.

nodes.label: DevOps and Observability for AI-Built Apps
nodes.title: DevOps and Observability for AI-Built Apps
nodes.search: DevOps and Observability for AI Built Apps Fourth workshop of AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp that adds DevOps practices to the AI built system design interview app: separate development and production environments, a CI/CD pipeline, and observability by instrumenting the FastAPI backend with OpenTelemetry to collect traces, error codes, and latency metrics on a monitoring dashboard.

nodes.label: Docker for Data Engineering: Postgres, Docker Compose, and Real-World Workflows
nodes.title: Docker for Data Engineering: Postgres, Docker Compose, and Real-World Workflows
nodes.search: Docker for Data Engineering: Postgres, Docker Compose, and Real World Workflows Refreshed Data Engineering Zoomcamp module 1 on Docker: containerizing a data ingestion workflow with Postgres, connecting with pgcli installed as a uv dev dependency, and using GitHub Codespaces as the recommended environment, with fixes for the setup problems students hit in past cohorts and Docker Compose for multi container workflows.

nodes.label: Doing Good with Data
nodes.title: Doing Good with Data
nodes.search: Doing Good with Data A senior data scientist at Capgemini traces how data science is applied for social good, drawing on her NGO work during the Ebola outbreak routing API data into dashboards that helped raise 15.6 million euros in emergency aid, and maps where data skills can do good today, from refugee response to volunteering.

nodes.label: Durable Agentic Workflows with Temporal.io
nodes.title: Durable Agentic Workflows with Temporal.io
nodes.search: Durable Agentic Workflows with Temporal.io Workshop on durable agentic workflows with Temporal: Alexey builds a deep research agent that ingests DataTalks.Club podcast episodes and subtitles, delegating steps like finding videos, searching Elasticsearch, and downloading transcripts to Temporal activities with timeouts and retries so the ingestion process is durable.

nodes.label: Economics and Automation Workshop: Building a Data Pipeline for Economic Insights
nodes.title: Economics and Automation Workshop: Building a Data Pipeline for Economic Insights
nodes.search: Economics and Automation Workshop: Building a Data Pipeline for Economic Insights Workshop, on 2024 12 02, with Ivan Brigida.

nodes.label: Effective Domain-Driven Design for Machine Learning Products
nodes.title: Effective Domain-Driven Design for Machine Learning Products
nodes.search: Effective Domain Driven Design for Machine Learning Products Workshop applying domain driven design to decide where machine learning genuinely belongs in a product: mapping the business process and external systems, marking pain points such as manual expense submission work, and deriving ML use case hypotheses from that shared understanding.

nodes.label: Effective Machine Learning Inside Your Database
nodes.title: Effective Machine Learning Inside Your Database
nodes.search: Effective Machine Learning Inside Your Database Hands on MindsDB workshop on doing machine learning inside the database: the benefits of keeping ML close to the data layer, declarative/AutoML pipelines that automate parts of the workflow, demos on supervised learning use cases, and extending MindsDB with additional ML frameworks.

nodes.label: Elevating RAG Systems
nodes.title: Elevating RAG Systems
nodes.search: Elevating RAG Systems Aula Misra's talk on taking RAG systems beyond the basic prototype, walking through the ingestion, retrieval, and generation pipelines with upgrades such as chunking strategies, query rewriting and routing, reranking, and prompt construction. It also covers production concerns including model gateways with fallbacks, PII guardrails, prompt compression, failure management with retries and human handoff, and caching.

nodes.label: Essential Communication Skills for Data Professionals
nodes.title: Essential Communication Skills for Data Professionals
nodes.search: Essential Communication Skills for Data Professionals The three communication skills data professionals need: simplifying difficult concepts, telling great stories, and presenting results confidently.

nodes.label: Evaluating AI Coding Agents with TeamCity and SWE-bench
nodes.title: Evaluating AI Coding Agents with TeamCity and SWE-bench
nodes.search: Evaluating AI Coding Agents with TeamCity and SWE bench JetBrains workshop on evaluating AI coding agents with SWE bench: Ernest (TeamCity product manager) explains what the benchmark actually measures — per task Docker environments checked out at the pre merge commit, a harness running the agent, and repo tests grading the result — and how JetBrains uses it to evaluate the agents they build.

nodes.label: Evaluation Store: a New Category of ML Engineering Tools
nodes.title: Evaluation Store: a New Category of ML Engineering Tools
nodes.search: Evaluation Store: a New Category of ML Engineering Tools Why model evaluation deserves its own tool category: the evaluation store, how it fits the existing ML toolchain, and what teams should evaluate and monitor once models reach production.

nodes.label: Fact-Checking with Wikidata
nodes.title: Fact-Checking with Wikidata
nodes.search: Fact Checking with Wikidata Wikimedia Deutschland workshop on fact checking LLM outputs with Wikidata: Philip introduces Wikidata's structured knowledge graph of items and statements, then queries items such as Einstein, extracts and filters hundreds of statements, and checks them against LLM claims to catch hallucinations.

nodes.label: FAQ Assistant in Practice: End-To-End Flow
nodes.title: FAQ Assistant in Practice: End-To-End Flow
nodes.search: FAQ Assistant in Practice: End To End Flow End to end walkthrough of the DataTalks.Club FAQ assistant: the FAQ dataset behind it, a Slack bot that answers course questions via a FAQ reaction or a direct trigger, and an agent assisted curation workflow that fixes malformed QnA entries and records GitHub commit IDs for each answer.

nodes.label: Feature Engineering for Time Series Forecasting
nodes.title: Feature Engineering for Time Series Forecasting
nodes.search: Feature Engineering for Time Series Forecasting Feature engineering techniques for time series forecasting, drawing on the presenter's forecasting and pricing work at Farfetch and contributions to statsmodels: constructing lag and seasonal features and other predictors from historical series to improve forecast models.

nodes.label: Feature Selection in Machine Learning with Python
nodes.title: Feature Selection in Machine Learning with Python
nodes.search: Feature Selection in Machine Learning with Python Feature selection methods in machine learning explained and demonstrated in Python by the maintainer of the feature engine package: filter, embedded, and wrapper approaches including feature shuffling to drop unimportant features, with demos built on scikit learn.

nodes.label: Federated Learning to the Rescue
nodes.title: Federated Learning to the Rescue
nodes.search: Federated Learning to the Rescue Using the Strava heatmap privacy leak as motivation, two Catulo engineers explain federated learning and its privacy rationale, arguing raw data should often not be shared or can barely be anonymized. They demo federated averaging training with the Flower framework on Kubeflow, packaging clients as Docker containers so teams can pick frameworks like PyTorch.

nodes.label: Fighting Fraud with Triplet Loss
nodes.title: Fighting Fraud with Triplet Loss
nodes.search: Fighting Fraud with Triplet Loss Detecting fake listings on classifieds sites with CNN embeddings and triplet loss: the fraud problem, hash generation from learned embeddings, and how to evaluate the approach.

nodes.label: Five Techniques for Improving RAG Chatbots
nodes.title: Five Techniques for Improving RAG Chatbots
nodes.search: Five Techniques for Improving RAG Chatbots Nikita, applied scientist in AWS's Generative AI Innovation Center, presents five techniques for improving the retrieval component of RAG chatbots, arguing quality comes from iterating on the whole system rather than just calling an LLM API. Techniques include hybrid search that runs vector and keyword retrieval in parallel, and query rewriting and expansion where a first LLM call reformulates noisy or follow up questions into concise search queries.

nodes.label: Foundations of Data Engineering Instruments
nodes.title: Foundations of Data Engineering Instruments
nodes.search: Foundations of Data Engineering Instruments Talk on database internals — binary search trees, B trees as used in PostgreSQL indexes, LSM trees, and copy on write as used in LMDB — piloted as a possible Data Engineering Zoomcamp module. It also contrasts OLTP and OLAP, row versus columnar storage, and data lake file formats with MapReduce techniques used by engines like Spark.

nodes.label: Fraud Detection in Financial Industry
nodes.title: Fraud Detection in Financial Industry
nodes.search: Fraud Detection in Financial Industry An introductory talk on fraud detection in finance covering AI use cases in banking (personalized recommendations, robo advice), types of fraud such as credit card fraud, phishing, and money laundering, and how models trained on large, quality datasets balance false positives and false negatives when flagging transactions.

nodes.label: Fraud Detection with Graph Features and GNN
nodes.title: Fraud Detection with Graph Features and GNN
nodes.search: Fraud Detection with Graph Features and GNN Lessons from five years of fraud detection work across banks, fintechs, and e commerce: why entity connections matter, engineering graph features, and applying graph neural networks (GNN) to fraud detection problems.

nodes.label: From APIs to Warehouses: AI-Assisted Data Ingestion with dlt
nodes.title: From APIs to Warehouses: AI-Assisted Data Ingestion with dlt
nodes.search: From APIs to Warehouses: AI Assisted Data Ingestion with dlt dltHub workshop on AI assisted data ingestion: Ashish introduces the dlt library for loading API data into warehouses and scaffolds a pipeline project, then wires a dlt MCP server into AI powered IDEs like Cursor and VS Code Copilot (with uv for the MCP setup) so the coding agent can build pipelines directly.

nodes.label: From Data to Deployment
nodes.title: From Data to Deployment
nodes.search: From Data to Deployment How to standardize machine learning lifecycles to move projects from data to deployment, structured around design, build, and monitoring phases, including data quality checks, model evaluation, and guidance on when an organization actually needs a feature store.

nodes.label: From Human-in-the-Loop to Agent-in-the-Loop: A Practical Transition Guide
nodes.title: From Human-in-the-Loop to Agent-in-the-Loop: A Practical Transition Guide
nodes.search: From Human in the Loop to Agent in the Loop: A Practical Transition Guide Theory focused webinar by researcher Art on transitioning from human in the loop to agent in the loop systems: it covers the motivation (ML systems scaling faster than human supervision), definitions and limitations of human in the loop, real agent in the loop examples and frameworks, and argues agents still need human oversight and feedback.

nodes.label: From RAG to Agents: Making Smart AI Assistants (LLM Zoomcamp bonus module)
nodes.title: From RAG to Agents: Making Smart AI Assistants (LLM Zoomcamp bonus module)
nodes.search: From RAG to Agents: Making Smart AI Assistants (LLM Zoomcamp bonus module) LLM Zoomcamp bonus module walking from basic RAG (minsearch, Elasticsearch, Qdrant) to agentic RAG, where the LLM issues iterative search queries in a loop and decides when it has enough context to answer. Implemented from scratch with prompts plus OpenAI function calling and no agent framework, it also shows how the same pattern scales to web search for deep research style systems.

nodes.label: From RAG to AI Agents: Function Calling and Tool Use
nodes.title: From RAG to AI Agents: Function Calling and Tool Use
nodes.search: From RAG to AI Agents: Function Calling and Tool Use LLM Zoomcamp session on moving from RAG to agents: it adds function calling to the FAQ assistant, showing how the model emits tool calls (such as a search function), how to parse the JSON arguments and dispatch the calls in Python, and how tool results feed back into the agent loop.

nodes.label: From REST to reasoning: ingest, index, and query with dlt and Cognee
nodes.title: From REST to reasoning: ingest, index, and query with dlt and Cognee
nodes.search: From REST to reasoning: ingest, index, and query with dlt and Cognee LLM Zoomcamp workshop that ingests REST API data (a NYC taxi dataset) with dlt and then uses Cognee to turn it into a queryable knowledge graph, with an LLM parsing raw records into entities, document chunks, and semantic connections organized by node sets. It includes a RAG refresher, a walkthrough of the generated graph, and cost notes for the underlying OpenAI calls.

nodes.label: Getting a Data Engineering Job
nodes.title: Getting a Data Engineering Job
nodes.search: Getting a Data Engineering Job Jeff of Jigsaw Labs explains how to land an entry level data engineering job: what data engineers actually do, building Python and SQL projects, reading the community's core books such as Designing Data Intensive Applications and Kimball, and networking into the data engineering community.

nodes.label: Getting Started with Network Analytics in Python
nodes.title: Getting Started with Network Analytics in Python
nodes.search: Getting Started with Network Analytics in Python A senior analyst at LendingTree gives a hands on introduction to network analysis in Python with NetworkX, covering nodes and edges, three ways to build a graph, directed and weighted graphs, and measuring node importance with three types of centrality.

nodes.label: GitOps for ML: Converting Notebooks to Reproducible Pipelines
nodes.title: GitOps for ML: Converting Notebooks to Reproducible Pipelines
nodes.search: GitOps for ML: Converting Notebooks to Reproducible Pipelines Workshop on converting a Jupyter notebook into a reproducible pipeline with DVC (data version control), structuring the prototype into pipeline stages, and taking model training online with CML, which brings CI/CD practices to machine learning.

nodes.label: Hands-on AI Observability
nodes.title: Hands-on AI Observability
nodes.search: Hands on AI Observability A hands on introduction to AI observability: instrumenting data and model behavior so ML applications can be monitored and trusted in production, demonstrated with Kensu.

nodes.label: Hands-On Data Monitoring with whylogs
nodes.title: Hands-On Data Monitoring with whylogs
nodes.search: Hands On Data Monitoring with whylogs A hands on workshop on data monitoring with the open source whylogs library, covering why production data pipelines break (schema changes, bugs, definition changes) and using whylogs data profiling in notebook examples for both batch and streaming systems.

nodes.label: Helping People Get Jobs with Data
nodes.title: Helping People Get Jobs with Data
nodes.search: Helping People Get Jobs with Data Padma, a senior manager in Indeed's enterprise data analytics group, shows how data powers a two sided job marketplace serving job seekers and employers, covering the data platform that moves Spark processed data from on prem Hadoop into cloud environments spanning AWS (Lambda, SQS, S3) and GCP (BigQuery), and the observability pipelines that bring resiliency and fault tolerance to their ETL work.

nodes.label: How to Boost Your Impact as A Data Professional
nodes.title: How to Boost Your Impact as A Data Professional
nodes.search: How to Boost Your Impact as A Data Professional Shahar, a data leader with 20 plus years including director of data engineering for trust and safety at Meta, shares how data professionals can boost their impact: the mindset of impact, a workflow for choosing what to work on, and building a mental model of how the business creates outcomes. He highlights data coverage, dogfooding your product, and reusable analytical patterns like ROI breakdowns and funnel analysis with conversion rates and dimensional cuts.

nodes.label: How to build an Agentic Search Flow
nodes.title: How to build an Agentic Search Flow
nodes.search: How to build an Agentic Search Flow A Jina AI engineer demonstrates an agentic search flow: hybrid search retrieves candidates and an agent loop evaluates the results and reformulates queries until it decides it has enough context, turning search from a single lookup into an iterative agent workflow.

nodes.label: How to Build an LLM-powered QA bot
nodes.title: How to Build an LLM-powered QA bot
nodes.search: How to Build an LLM powered QA bot Alex, a healthcare software engineer, explains how he built the LLM powered Zoomcamp QA bot that answers student questions in the DataTalks.Club Slack using RAG. The pipeline ingests FAQ documents and Slack threads parsed into question answer documents, orchestrates ingestion with Prefect and LangChain/LlamaIndex, caches embeddings, and stores vectors in Pinecone and later Zilliz Cloud (Milvus) for semantic search.

nodes.label: How to Evaluate MCP-powered AI Agents Beyond Accuracy using Agent GPA
nodes.title: How to Evaluate MCP-powered AI Agents Beyond Accuracy using Agent GPA
nodes.search: How to Evaluate MCP powered AI Agents Beyond Accuracy using Agent GPA Josh (Snowflake, previously of TruEra) on evaluating MCP powered agents beyond accuracy: he connects a LangGraph multi server MCP client to a Snowflake MCP server exposing PubMed and clinical trial search tools, calls Claude Sonnet through Snowflake Cortex, and introduces the Agent GPA approach for evaluating agent behavior beyond simple answer accuracy.

nodes.label: How to Land Your First Data Engineer Job
nodes.title: How to Land Your First Data Engineer Job
nodes.search: How to Land Your First Data Engineer Job Recruiter Gonzalo, CEO of a recruitment agency with a decade of hiring data scientists and engineers at companies like Feedzai and Mercedes Benz, explains how to land a first data engineer job from the recruiter's standpoint. He covers preparing the job search before polishing CV and LinkedIn, auditing your skills, leveraging your network, and interview tactics such as researching the company and interviewer and having questions ready.

nodes.label: How to use AI in Consumer Food Product Innovation
nodes.title: How to use AI in Consumer Food Product Innovation
nodes.search: How to use AI in Consumer Food Product Innovation How AI already surrounds consumer products, from card fraud detection to image analytics, and what the AI, ML, and DL distinction means for consumer food product innovation.

nodes.label: How to Work with AI Coding Agents: Spec-Driven Development, Context and Loop Engineering, Workflows
nodes.title: How to Work with AI Coding Agents: Spec-Driven Development, Context and Loop Engineering, Workflows
nodes.search: How to Work with AI Coding Agents: Spec Driven Development, Context and Loop Engineering, Workflows Opening workshop of AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp on AI native development: spec driven development, context engineering, and loop/graph engineering, demonstrated by building a project with Claude Code or Codex, organizing work as GitHub issues, and running a team of agents (product manager, implementer, tester). Alexey notes the full process costs roughly 4 5x more tokens per issue but yields better quality because the tester agent catches things the implementer misses.

nodes.label: How to write data pipelines with Apache Airflow® 3.0
nodes.title: How to write data pipelines with Apache Airflow® 3.0
nodes.search: How to write data pipelines with Apache Airflow® 3.0 Hands on workshop on Apache Airflow 3.0 led by Tim Davis of Astronomer, covering Airflow's history and new 3.0 features with a demo built using the Astro CLI. It demonstrates DAG versioning, backfills, remote execution, cross resource workflows, and pitfalls when upgrading from Airflow 2 to 3.

nodes.label: How Your Machine Learning Project Will Fail
nodes.title: How Your Machine Learning Project Will Fail
nodes.search: How Your Machine Learning Project Will Fail Why machine learning projects stall between proof of concept and production: scoping mistakes, how traditional industries differ from tech companies, and the deployment gap in AI adoption.

nodes.label: Hypothesis Testing: Bayesian or Frequentist? Two ways of looking at the same coin
nodes.title: Hypothesis Testing: Bayesian or Frequentist? Two ways of looking at the same coin
nodes.search: Hypothesis Testing: Bayesian or Frequentist? Two ways of looking at the same coin A practitioner compares frequentist and Bayesian approaches to hypothesis testing on the coin flip problem behind clicks and conversions, walking through the binomial test, Bayesian parameter estimation, and Bayes factors, and argues the Bayesian route is often more practical.

nodes.label: Identity Resolution Essentials from a Data Scientist
nodes.title: Identity Resolution Essentials from a Data Scientist
nodes.search: Identity Resolution Essentials from a Data Scientist A data scientist's guide to identity resolution: deterministic vs probabilistic matching and their precision/reach trade off, use cases unlocked by unified customer identity graphs, the team's experience building identity resolution in house, and how Segment Unifi addresses it.

nodes.label: Implement a Search Engine
nodes.title: Implement a Search Engine
nodes.search: Implement a Search Engine Pre course LLM Zoomcamp workshop building a toy in memory search engine (minsearch) over course FAQ documents, explaining text search fundamentals like tokenization and TF IDF with scikit learn vectorizers. It scores queries with cosine similarity across weighted text fields and applies post filtering by course, laying the retrieval groundwork for the RAG system built in the course.

nodes.label: Industrial Applications of Reinforcement Learning
nodes.title: Industrial Applications of Reinforcement Learning
nodes.search: Industrial Applications of Reinforcement Learning An accessible introduction to reinforcement learning from the O'Reilly book author, using reward based training analogies to explain how academic advances reach industrial applications.

nodes.label: Ingesting Agent Traces with dlthub
nodes.title: Ingesting Agent Traces with dlthub
nodes.search: Ingesting Agent Traces with dlthub Hands on dltHub workshop (part of LLM Zoomcamp) on ingesting agent traces: coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Copilot store session metadata locally, and the session uses dlt to load that data and build a local dashboard of token usage, then extends the same approach to collecting traces from a deployed assistant.

nodes.label: Ingestion and Historization in the Data Lake
nodes.title: Ingestion and Historization in the Data Lake
nodes.search: Ingestion and Historization in the Data Lake Walks through building a data lake ingestion and historization pipeline: AWS DMS extracts DynamoDB source tables into S3, a PySpark job on EMR applies SCD type 2 historization (valid from/valid to fields, date based partitioning for tables over 1 GB), and Athena serves ad hoc SQL checks, all scheduled and monitored with Airflow.

nodes.label: Introduction to Bayesian Inference for Parameter Estimation
nodes.title: Introduction to Bayesian Inference for Parameter Estimation
nodes.search: Introduction to Bayesian Inference for Parameter Estimation Introduction to Bayesian inference for parameter estimation: priors, likelihoods, and posteriors worked through a coin toss example, solved analytically and by simulation with PyMC, plus discussion of when Bayesian estimation beats classical t tests and p value hypothesis testing.

nodes.label: Introduction to Data Engineering Zoomcamp
nodes.title: Introduction to Data Engineering Zoomcamp
nodes.search: Introduction to Data Engineering Zoomcamp Introduction and Q&A for the 2024 Data Engineering Zoomcamp, where Alexey Grigorev covers prerequisites (basic Python and SQL), urges installing Docker early, and presents the new Terraform videos while explaining why Airflow was dropped in favor of Mage, with any orchestrator allowed in projects. He also explains capstone project rules — two attempts, peer review, and using projects as portfolio pieces for job hunting — plus environment setup advice.

nodes.label: Introduction to ML Engineering and ML Zoomcamp
nodes.title: Introduction to ML Engineering and ML Zoomcamp
nodes.search: Introduction to ML Engineering and ML Zoomcamp Introduction to the Machine Learning Zoomcamp course and what it takes to become a machine learning engineer: part one covers ML fundamentals (regression, classification, evaluation, decision trees, neural networks with Keras/TensorFlow) and part two covers deploying trained models as web services, followed by signup logistics and Q&A.

nodes.label: Introduction to MLOps and MLOps Zoomcamp
nodes.title: Introduction to MLOps and MLOps Zoomcamp
nodes.search: Introduction to MLOps and MLOps Zoomcamp Introduction to MLOps framed as a design train operate lifecycle for ML projects, explaining where practices like experiment tracking, deployment, and monitoring fit, followed by a walkthrough of what the free MLOps Zoomcamp course covers.

nodes.label: Introduction to NLP for Industry Use
nodes.title: Introduction to NLP for Industry Use
nodes.search: Introduction to NLP for Industry Use An engineering manager at Persona surveys modern NLP from LSTM milestones to GPT 3 few shot learning, then covers how NLP projects are built in industry, the tradeoffs of neural models such as unpredictable errors and data hungry fixes, and how to hire and manage a solid NLP team.

nodes.label: Introduction to Transformers for NLP
nodes.title: Introduction to Transformers for NLP
nodes.search: Introduction to Transformers for NLP An introduction to the transformers behind modern NLP that builds up from tokens and pretrained word embeddings such as word2vec and GloVe, through RNNs and sequence to sequence machine translation, to the encoder decoder attention architecture.

nodes.label: Introduction to Vibe Coding: Build a Game with AI
nodes.title: Introduction to Vibe Coding: Build a Game with AI
nodes.search: Introduction to Vibe Coding: Build a Game with AI Introduction to vibe coding (AI assisted development) that surveys tool categories — chat assistants like ChatGPT, IDE assistants like GitHub Copilot and Cursor, project bootstrappers like Lovable, and agents — while building a React snake game with AI help. It demonstrates iterating through prompts, committing working code before AI edits, and AI assisted debugging, serving as module one of the planned AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp.

nodes.label: Keeping Your Model In Production
nodes.title: Keeping Your Model In Production
nodes.search: Keeping Your Model In Production Workshop on keeping ML models healthy in production using Arize: detecting data and concept drift, analyzing embeddings, and using dashboards to monitor model performance, drawing on the instructor's ML observability course material.

nodes.label: Large Language Models Agents
nodes.title: Large Language Models Agents
nodes.search: Large Language Models Agents Workshop on LLM based agents that starts from transformer/LLM fundamentals and covers agent paradigms, prompting, fine tuning including RLHF and parameter efficient tuning with Hugging Face models, and evaluation approaches such as public benchmarks, human annotation, user testing, and LLM as judge.

nodes.label: LLM Zoomcamp 2024 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.title: LLM Zoomcamp 2024 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.search: LLM Zoomcamp 2024 Pre Course Live Q&A Pre course Q&A for LLM Zoomcamp 2024: prerequisites (Python and command line, no prior ML needed, LLMs treated as black boxes), using an OpenAI API key alongside local open source models, the syllabus (Q&A systems, text and vector search engines, RAG, Docker), capstone projects, and how the Slack community supports students.

nodes.label: LLM Zoomcamp 2025
nodes.title: LLM Zoomcamp 2025
nodes.search: LLM Zoomcamp 2025 Pre course live Q&A for the 2025 LLM Zoomcamp cohort, where Alexey Grigorev outlines curriculum changes: dropping the open source module (becoming a separate course), splitting evaluation and monitoring into two modules, adopting Phoenix for monitoring instead of Grafana, and possibly a new vector search tool. He also covers prerequisites, capstone expectations, navigating the GitHub repo, and repeated questions about an agents module.

nodes.label: LLM Zoomcamp 2026 Course Launch
nodes.title: LLM Zoomcamp 2026 Course Launch
nodes.search: LLM Zoomcamp 2026 Course Launch Launch session for the free 10 week LLM Zoomcamp 2026: a tour of the GitHub repo and course platform, an outline of the syllabus (RAG, vector search, orchestration, agents, evaluation, and monitoring for a knowledge base assistant), and answers to logistics questions.

nodes.label: LLM Zoomcamp 2026 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.title: LLM Zoomcamp 2026 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.search: LLM Zoomcamp 2026 Pre Course Live Q&A Pre course live Q&A for LLM Zoomcamp 2026 covering logistics, prerequisites, and the practical RAG focused syllabus — building an assistant that answers questions over a knowledge base — plus agents, with a free form capstone project on any dataset except the course FAQ data.

nodes.label: LLM Zoomcamp Course Launch
nodes.title: LLM Zoomcamp Course Launch
nodes.search: LLM Zoomcamp Course Launch Launch stream for the LLM Zoomcamp cohort starting in June, covering prerequisites (Python, command line, Docker), the instructor team, and modules including vector search with Qdrant, best practices, and LLM monitoring with Phoenix. It also explains cohort logistics such as leaderboards, learning in public points, and getting help through Slack, the FAQ, and the course bot.

nodes.label: Load Testing ML Microservices for Robustness and Scalability
nodes.title: Load Testing ML Microservices for Robustness and Scalability
nodes.search: Load Testing ML Microservices for Robustness and Scalability Emmanuel Raj, lead machine learning engineer and author of Engineering MLOps, demonstrates load testing ML microservices with Locust in Docker and Kubernetes to validate robustness and scalability before taking models to production.

nodes.label: Machine Learning Design Patterns
nodes.title: Machine Learning Design Patterns
nodes.search: Machine Learning Design Patterns A tour of machine learning design patterns from the catalog of thirty in the book by Google practitioners, walking through rebalancing for dataset preparation and two productionizing patterns with tradeoffs and alternatives.

nodes.label: Machine Learning for Customer Service
nodes.title: Machine Learning for Customer Service
nodes.search: Machine Learning for Customer Service Machine learning at Monzo, the app only UK bank: how the ML team's work evolved from the banking license days through growth to nearly five million customers.

nodes.label: Machine Learning in Digital Identity
nodes.title: Machine Learning in Digital Identity
nodes.search: Machine Learning in Digital Identity How Veriff applies machine learning to digital identity verification: biometric face verification, computer vision checks for document tampering and fraud, and how an ML product manager combines these models with business logic and product decisions.

nodes.label: Machine Learning Observability
nodes.title: Machine Learning Observability
nodes.search: Machine Learning Observability An ML observability overview by the founder of Arize (previously on Uber's Michelangelo platform) covering production monitoring of models: drift metrics such as PSI, KL divergence, and Wasserstein distance, data quality checks like cardinality and type mismatch, and global, cohort, and individual level explainability with SHAP and LIME.

nodes.label: Machine Learning Performance Monitoring
nodes.title: Machine Learning Performance Monitoring
nodes.search: Machine Learning Performance Monitoring Practical model monitoring from Evidently AI's CTO: analyzing production ML model performance across industries from banking to manufacturing and the tooling for monitoring model quality.

nodes.label: Machine Learning with Ray: Supercharge Your GPU Clusters
nodes.title: Machine Learning with Ray: Supercharge Your GPU Clusters
nodes.search: Machine Learning with Ray: Supercharge Your GPU Clusters Demonstrates Ray for distributed machine learning: why distributed GPU compute is needed, the Ray core programming model (ray.remote tasks, futures, resource decorators) and libraries like Ray Train and Ray Data, plus a live demo running a PyTorch MNIST training job on a two GPU Ray cluster on Genesis Cloud with the Ray dashboard, and discussion of Kubernetes integration and data vs model parallelism.

nodes.label: Machine Learning Workflows in Production
nodes.title: Machine Learning Workflows in Production
nodes.search: Machine Learning Workflows in Production How Zalando's ML productivity team standardizes workflows from experimentation to production: JupyterHub and GPU/HPC resources for fast iteration, ML pipelines authored as Metaflow scripts that generate CloudFormation templates deployed via GitHub, and a Backstage based ML platform plugin for observability and debugging.

nodes.label: Make Data Magical with Mage
nodes.title: Make Data Magical with Mage
nodes.search: Make Data Magical with Mage Workshop on leveling up data transformation with Mage, an open source pipeline tool, situating it in the evolving modern data stack alongside dbt, Airflow, and SQLMesh, and demonstrating dbt based transformation workflows inside Mage.

nodes.label: Make Your First ML Chatbot
nodes.title: Make Your First ML Chatbot
nodes.search: Make Your First ML Chatbot A Rasa walkthrough of building your first ML chatbot, covering a brief NLP history, how task oriented dialogue systems differ from open domain chitchat bots, and the core components: NLU intent and entity recognition, dialogue policies, and evaluation to improve conversations over time.

nodes.label: Maximizing Confidence in Your Data Model Changes with dbt and PipeRider
nodes.title: Maximizing Confidence in Your Data Model Changes with dbt and PipeRider
nodes.search: Maximizing Confidence in Your Data Model Changes with dbt and PipeRider Workshop on maximizing confidence in dbt model changes with PipeRider: what better code review for data projects looks like, using PipeRider's data profiles to compare state before and after model changes, with DuckDB as the demo warehouse as part of the Data Engineering Zoomcamp workshop series.

nodes.label: Mitigating Bias with the XAI Toolbox
nodes.title: Mitigating Bias with the XAI Toolbox
nodes.search: Mitigating Bias with the XAI Toolbox Serg Masis, data scientist at Syngenta and author of a Packt book on interpretable machine learning, explains explainable AI and the origins of dataset bias, then live codes quantifying bias on a census income dataset with fairness measures like statistical parity difference and disparate impact and demonstrates mitigation approaches.

nodes.label: ML Zoomcamp 2024 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.title: ML Zoomcamp 2024 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.search: ML Zoomcamp 2024 Pre Course Live Q&A Pre course live Q&A for the 2024 Machine Learning Zoomcamp cohort starting September 16, where Alexey Grigorev answers questions on prerequisites, project rules (covering any extra techniques like GNNs yourself), certificates, homework points, and deadlines. He notes most content is pre recorded with no weekly live sessions and recommends past years' office hour playlists as supplementary material.

nodes.label: ML Zoomcamp 2025 Course Launch
nodes.title: ML Zoomcamp 2025 Course Launch
nodes.search: ML Zoomcamp 2025 Course Launch Launch stream for the fifth Machine Learning Zoomcamp cohort, where Alexey Grigorev presents the syllabus, prerequisites (coding and command line comfort, no prior ML required), homework and capstone structure, leaderboards, and Slack guidelines. It also encourages learning in public, citing graduates who attracted recruiters and internship opportunities by sharing their progress.

nodes.label: ML Zoomcamp 2025 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.title: ML Zoomcamp 2025 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.search: ML Zoomcamp 2025 Pre Course Live Q&A Pre course live Q&A for the fifth Machine Learning Zoomcamp cohort, where Alexey Grigorev answers questions on prerequisites, the partially updated syllabus (including a PyTorch option for the deep learning module), homework deadlines, certificates, and cohort logistics. He explains the course focuses on ML engineering and deployment rather than deep computer vision or RAG, pointing RAG questions to LLM Zoomcamp.

nodes.label: ML Zoomcamp 2026 Course Launch
nodes.title: ML Zoomcamp 2026 Course Launch
nodes.search: ML Zoomcamp 2026 Course Launch Webinar, on 2026 09 14, with Alexey Grigorev.

nodes.label: ML Zoomcamp 2026 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.title: ML Zoomcamp 2026 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.search: ML Zoomcamp 2026 Pre Course Live Q&A Pre course Q&A for ML Zoomcamp 2026 covering the syllabus (regression and classification with scikit learn, XGBoost, PyTorch deep learning, then serving with FastAPI on AWS Lambda and Kubernetes), positioning the course as an introduction to machine learning engineering, advice on choosing between AI engineering, ML engineering, and data engineering by building portfolio projects in industries you target, the AI usage policy, and the three project certificate rule.

nodes.label: MLOps Zoomcamp - Experiment Tracking with Weights and Biases
nodes.title: MLOps Zoomcamp - Experiment Tracking with Weights and Biases
nodes.search: MLOps Zoomcamp Experiment Tracking with Weights and Biases MLOps Zoomcamp module 2 workshop showing experiment tracking with Weights & Biases as an alternative to MLflow: logging runs, dataset and model versioning with artifacts, interactive tables and dashboards, reports, and hyperparameter optimization.

nodes.label: MLOps Zoomcamp 2024 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.title: MLOps Zoomcamp 2024 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.search: MLOps Zoomcamp 2024 Pre Course Live Q&A Pre course live Q&A for the MLOps Zoomcamp 2024 cohort, where Alexey Grigorev clarifies the course targets ML engineers rather than data engineers, points Docker beginners to ML Zoomcamp's deployment module, and advises choosing MLOps tools by use case since the underlying concepts transfer. He also covers Codespaces as an environment option, the MLOps job market, and learning in public for job seekers.

nodes.label: MLOps Zoomcamp 2025 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.title: MLOps Zoomcamp 2025 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.search: MLOps Zoomcamp 2025 Pre Course Live Q&A Pre course Q&A for the MLOps Zoomcamp 2025 cohort starting May 5, where Alexey Grigorev says content stays mostly the same except a reworked orchestration module, and cloud spend is optional though a small AWS account helps for streaming deployment with Kinesis and Lambda. He also covers Docker prerequisites (pointing to ML Zoomcamp module 5), the ML engineer and data scientist roles the course fits, and how the free courses are sponsored.

nodes.label: MLOps Zoomcamp Competition - Bot or Not?
nodes.title: MLOps Zoomcamp Competition - Bot or Not?
nodes.search: MLOps Zoomcamp Competition Bot or Not? The MLOps Zoomcamp Bot or Not competition runs a Streamlit Turing test platform where students deploy chatbots with the full MLOps stack, including Docker, Kubernetes, GitOps, and monitoring, and earn a leaderboard score by how long human players fail to detect them.

nodes.label: Modeling the Human Brain
nodes.title: Modeling the Human Brain
nodes.search: Modeling the Human Brain A cognitive neuroscience PhD candidate at UC Irvine shows how neuroscientists apply data science and network science to brain imaging, from MRI basics to modeling the brain as a complex graph to predict brain age and detect disease before manifestation.

nodes.label: Modern Data Pipelines in AdTech - Life in the Trenches
nodes.title: Modern Data Pipelines in AdTech - Life in the Trenches
nodes.search: Modern Data Pipelines in AdTech Life in the Trenches Inside modern AdTech data pipelines at Captify: Spark jobs that join log level impressions, clicks, and conversions with Postgres enriched reference data into Parquet on HDFS and S3, plus the practical challenges of historical data reprocessing.

nodes.label: Modern Data Stack for Analytics Engineering
nodes.title: Modern Data Stack for Analytics Engineering
nodes.search: Modern Data Stack for Analytics Engineering A senior analytics engineer at SeatGeek tours the modern data stack (extraction/loading tools, cloud data warehouses, orchestration, observability, and BI tools like Looker, Tableau, Metabase, and Lightdash) and demos dbt: defining models in SQL and YAML, materializations (table, view, ephemeral as CTEs), and schema tests such as unique and not null checks.

nodes.label: Modern Data Warehouse
nodes.title: Modern Data Warehouse
nodes.search: Modern Data Warehouse A data engineering leader contrasts traditional data warehouse architecture with the modern data warehouse, explaining how larger volumes, new data sources, data lakes, streaming ingestion, ELT with dbt, and data science/ML consumers reshape warehouse design.

nodes.label: Monitoring LLM Applications: Traces, Feedback, and Production Quality
nodes.title: Monitoring LLM Applications: Traces, Feedback, and Production Quality
nodes.search: Monitoring LLM Applications: Traces, Feedback, and Production Quality LLM Zoomcamp workshop on monitoring GenAI applications: a simple RAG app logs every user interaction to a Postgres database, a Streamlit dashboard displays statistics such as conversation counts, average response time, and token cost per request, and a Grafana dashboard is added on top for production style monitoring.

nodes.label: Monitoring Model Performance with Crowdsourcing
nodes.title: Monitoring Model Performance with Crowdsourcing
nodes.search: Monitoring Model Performance with Crowdsourcing A Toloka data evangelist runs a hands on workshop on using the crowdsourcing platform to monitor machine learning model performance, showing how to collect human labels on production style tasks and compare them against model predictions to track performance.

nodes.label: n8n: From Fundamentals to Building Intelligent Automation Pipeline
nodes.title: n8n: From Fundamentals to Building Intelligent Automation Pipeline
nodes.search: n8n: From Fundamentals to Building Intelligent Automation Pipeline n8n workshop (AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp automation module) on low code AI automation: building intelligent pipelines such as a LinkedIn writer agent, a resume to PDF job tool, and Telegram notifications by wiring app nodes (Postgres, Airtable, AWS) and LLM steps without hand writing API integrations, plus notes on deploying workflows with Docker.

nodes.label: Notebooks in Production - Fun or not Fun?
nodes.title: Notebooks in Production - Fun or not Fun?
nodes.search: Notebooks in Production Fun or not Fun? A staff data engineer at Delivery Hero shares lessons from running notebooks in production, where data scientists ship parameterized training jobs with Papermill orchestrated by Airflow across 15 countries, covering the benefits of fast delivery cycles and easy onboarding and the limits for complex models.

nodes.label: Observing Python Applications Using Prometheus
nodes.title: Observing Python Applications Using Prometheus
nodes.search: Observing Python Applications Using Prometheus Hands on workshop on observing Python applications with Prometheus: exposing metrics endpoints, understanding counters and labels, and adding custom metrics such as request counts by status code and endpoint to monitor live services.

nodes.label: Open source data ingestion for RAGs with dlt
nodes.title: Open source data ingestion for RAGs with dlt
nodes.search: Open source data ingestion for RAGs with dlt An LLM Zoomcamp workshop by a dltHub solutions engineer on building a scalable RAG ingestion pipeline with open source dlt: data ingestion challenges, configuring a dlt REST API source to pull Notion pages and blocks with secrets in environment variables, loading into LanceDB for vector search, and syncing changes on a schedule.

nodes.label: Open Source MLOps on Public Cloud
nodes.title: Open Source MLOps on Public Cloud
nodes.search: Open Source MLOps on Public Cloud Workshop on running open source MLOps on public cloud with Kubeflow: Canonical's Charmed Kubeflow distribution and an AWS Marketplace appliance that reduce setup from thousands of lines of YAML to a few commands, then creating notebooks and pipelines on Kubernetes.

nodes.label: Open-Source LLM Zoomcamp 2025
nodes.title: Open-Source LLM Zoomcamp 2025
nodes.search: Open Source LLM Zoomcamp 2025 Pre course Q&A for the new Open Source LLM Zoomcamp mini course, split out of LLM Zoomcamp's open source module, covering running and serving open models such as DeepSeek R1 distill on cloud GPUs provided by AMD and Saturn Cloud plus a fine tuning module. Alexey Grigorev also answers questions on prerequisites, model size versus GPU memory, and recommends portfolio projects over books for landing entry level data and ML roles.

nodes.label: Orchestrating Enterprise ML Workload Jobs Across Clouds
nodes.title: Orchestrating Enterprise ML Workload Jobs Across Clouds
nodes.search: Orchestrating Enterprise ML Workload Jobs Across Clouds A former AWS SageMaker product manager and Intuit's former head of ML platform engineering discuss orchestrating enterprise ML workloads across tools and cloud platforms, arguing that large organizations end up integrating multiple specialized platforms rather than standardizing on a single end to end tool.

nodes.label: Paradoxes in Data Science
nodes.title: Paradoxes in Data Science
nodes.search: Paradoxes in Data Science Webinar, on 2021 11 23, with Pier Paolo Ippolito.

nodes.label: Practical guide: Fine-tuning Qwen3 with LoRA
nodes.title: Practical guide: Fine-tuning Qwen3 with LoRA
nodes.search: Practical guide: Fine tuning Qwen3 with LoRA Workshop on parameter efficient fine tuning of Qwen3, covering the progression from prompt engineering to soft prompting and LoRA using Hugging Face PEFT, Transformers, TRL, and bitsandbytes on a single local CUDA GPU. It demonstrates preparing instruction datasets such as Databricks Dolly 15k, quantization choices (int4/int8), and setting up baseline experiments to tune hyperparameters like LoRA rank.

nodes.label: Practical Learning-to-Rank: Deep, Fast, Precise
nodes.title: Practical Learning-to-Rank: Deep, Fast, Precise
nodes.search: Practical Learning to Rank: Deep, Fast, Precise Practical learning to rank for search, recommendations, and feeds: why ranking differs from plain binary classification, how implicit feedback like clicks and viewport tracking becomes training labels, and a MovieLens based recommender demo with the open source Metarank tool.

nodes.label: Probabilistic Demand Forecasting at Scale
nodes.title: Probabilistic Demand Forecasting at Scale
nodes.search: Probabilistic Demand Forecasting at Scale An applied scientist's view of probabilistic demand forecasting at scale, sitting at the intersection of economics, forecasting, and deep learning: probabilistic and transformer based methods such as quantile forecasts, inventory and supply chain relevance, and open research areas.

nodes.label: Productionizing a Feature Store for Fraud Detection at Ubisoft
