nodes.title: Productionizing a Feature Store for Fraud Detection at Ubisoft
nodes.search: Productionizing a Feature Store for Fraud Detection at Ubisoft A machine learning data engineer at Ubisoft recounts productionizing a feature store for fraud detection on the company's e commerce platform, tracing the evolution from a SQL based v1 through an optimized PySpark v1.5 to a v2 design that keeps offline and online feature definitions aligned and generates features incrementally.

nodes.label: Productionizing ML Systems without Fear nor Heroism
nodes.title: Productionizing ML Systems without Fear nor Heroism
nodes.search: Productionizing ML Systems without Fear nor Heroism A machine learning engineer and author shows how software engineering best practices transfer to productionizing ML systems, focusing on three data centric practices: data versioning, unit tests for data, and data monitoring.

nodes.label: Prompt Engineering 101
nodes.title: Prompt Engineering 101
nodes.search: Prompt Engineering 101 Prompt Engineering 101 covering the basics of getting precise results from ChatGPT: two core principles of good prompting, practical tips and tricks like role/persona assignment and step by step instructions, model limitations, and how the presenter uses ChatGPT in his own work.

nodes.label: Putting Data Science in Production
nodes.title: Putting Data Science in Production
nodes.search: Putting Data Science in Production What it takes to move the standard notebook workflow of Jupyter, scikit learn, and pandas into production, and the tooling and practices beyond the core modeling loop.

nodes.label: PyTorch Contributor's Guide: How and Why?
nodes.title: PyTorch Contributor's Guide: How and Why?
nodes.search: PyTorch Contributor's Guide: How and Why? A research engineer explains why contributing to open source builds developer confidence and teamwork skills, then gives a practical PyTorch contributor's guide: how the project is organized, how to find and pick issues to resolve, and the technical realities of landing a first contribution.

nodes.label: RAG and Agents Evaluation: Measuring Retrieval and LLM Answer Quality
nodes.title: RAG and Agents Evaluation: Measuring Retrieval and LLM Answer Quality
nodes.search: RAG and Agents Evaluation: Measuring Retrieval and LLM Answer Quality LLM Zoomcamp module on evaluating RAG and agents: offline evaluation of the FAQ assistant's retrieval using relevance matrices and metrics such as hit rate, plus measurement of the quality of the LLM's generated answers, demonstrated on the course's running FAQ example.

nodes.label: RAG in Action: Next-Level Retrieval Augmented Generation
nodes.title: RAG in Action: Next-Level Retrieval Augmented Generation
nodes.search: RAG in Action: Next Level Retrieval Augmented Generation A Kern AI solution architect presents a data centric approach to RAG, covering common failure modes, hands on use of Kern AI's Refinery and bricks tools to chunk text with spaCy and embed it with E5 embedding models (chosen via the Hugging Face MTEB leaderboard), and tips such as adding reranking/cross encoder models and handling tabular data in RAG pipelines.

nodes.label: Recommender Systems for Digital Advertising
nodes.title: Recommender Systems for Digital Advertising
nodes.search: Recommender Systems for Digital Advertising A senior data scientist working on digital out of home advertising formulates ad recommendation for mall billboard networks as a probabilistic model, then shows how to measure the business impact of adopting a recommender by clustering screen locations into balanced test and control groups and running survey based experiments.

nodes.label: Reinforcement Learning for Search
nodes.title: Reinforcement Learning for Search
nodes.search: Reinforcement Learning for Search How Findify applies reinforcement learning to ranking in white label e commerce search, covering the path from academic research to production relevance, product listings, and recommendations.

nodes.label: Running Durable Agents in Production
nodes.title: Running Durable Agents in Production
nodes.search: Running Durable Agents in Production Workshop on durable agents in production using the Conductor orchestration engine: Nicholas defines durable execution, shows agents and tools defined in Python being compiled into workflows, and demonstrates execution views that expose each step's input, output, token usage, and failure states for a billing agent that makes LLM calls and tool calls.

nodes.label: Setting Up AI Projects for Success
nodes.title: Setting Up AI Projects for Success
nodes.search: Setting Up AI Projects for Success The head of AI at Volkswagen's software agency CARIAD lays out frameworks and guardrails for setting up AI projects for success, covering how to come up with AI project ideas, evaluate and scope them, and deliver them successfully.

nodes.label: Setting up an A/B Testing Framework
nodes.title: Setting up an A/B Testing Framework
nodes.search: Setting up an A/B Testing Framework Webinar, on 2021 05 04, with Agnes van Belle.

nodes.label: Software Testing for Machine Learning Pipelines
nodes.title: Software Testing for Machine Learning Pipelines
nodes.search: Software Testing for Machine Learning Pipelines A machine learning engineer draws on a costly production bug to explain how software engineering testing practices such as unit and integration tests with coverage, combined with ML specific testing approaches, make machine learning pipelines robust enough for real systems with loads and corner cases.

nodes.label: Speeding up Python Code 500x
nodes.title: Speeding up Python Code 500x
nodes.search: Speeding up Python Code 500x The design rework behind the major version bump of whylogs, an open source Python library that profiles data for ML monitoring: splitting columns by type into mini batches, selective computation, and using Apache DataSketches to cut Python to C++ calls, yielding order of magnitude profiling speedups.

nodes.label: Stock Market Analytics Zoomcamp 2025 - Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.title: Stock Market Analytics Zoomcamp 2025 - Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.search: Stock Market Analytics Zoomcamp 2025 Pre Course Live Q&A Pre launch Q&A for the second Stock Market Analytics Zoomcamp, hosted by instructor Ivan Brigida (BI analyst at Google) and Alexey Grigorev, covering the registrant survey, prerequisites, syllabus, homework format, and leaderboard mechanics. They stress the course is educational rather than investment advice and encourage learning in public on LinkedIn and other platforms.

nodes.label: Stock Market Analytics Zoomcamp Pre-Launch Q&A
nodes.title: Stock Market Analytics Zoomcamp Pre-Launch Q&A
nodes.search: Stock Market Analytics Zoomcamp Pre Launch Q&A Pre launch Q&A for the first Stock Market Analytics Zoomcamp cohort starting April 15, 2024, a course created with instructor Ivan Brigida after a DataTalks.Club podcast episode on analytics and stock markets. They present registrant survey results, course logistics, leaderboard points for learning in public, and a tour of the Slack community.

nodes.label: Stock Markets Analytics Zoomcamp 2026 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.title: Stock Markets Analytics Zoomcamp 2026 Pre-Course Live Q&A
nodes.search: Stock Markets Analytics Zoomcamp 2026 Pre Course Live Q&A Pre course live Q&A for Stock Markets Analytics Zoomcamp 2026 where instructor Ivan (a BI analyst at Google with finance and CS background) walks through the syllabus, questionnaire results, and logistics, and explains how much Python and finance background students need. He also describes using his own prediction system as partial automation while keeping the final buy/sell decision manual at the broker.

nodes.label: Stream Processing
nodes.title: Stream Processing
nodes.search: Stream Processing A RisingWave engineer teaches stream processing in SQL, contrasting batch and streaming execution, and demos incremental computation in RisingWave: Kafka ingestion, stateless and stateful streaming operators, materialized views built on materialized views, dynamic filters for time varying predicates, and reading query plans, on an NYC taxi dataset with a follow up homework.

nodes.label: Stream Processing with PyFlink
nodes.title: Stream Processing with PyFlink
nodes.search: Stream Processing with PyFlink Data Engineering Zoomcamp streaming module taught with Kafka and PyFlink: producing events to Kafka topics, consuming them, and inserting processed ride records into Postgres, demonstrating end to end stream processing where data lands in the database immediately after it is sent.

nodes.label: System Design in Data Engineering
nodes.title: System Design in Data Engineering
nodes.search: System Design in Data Engineering A CTO and head of data at a UK fintech startup explains data engineering system design interviews: what interviewers assess for seniority, walking through a worked example of designing an ETL system for a social media platform (clarifying requirements, estimating data volumes, medallion layers, and dual running migrations with a consumer switchover), and recommending Designing Data Intensive Applications plus System Design Interview books for preparation.

nodes.label: Terraform: Reshaping the Data Engineering Experience
nodes.title: Terraform: Reshaping the Data Engineering Experience
nodes.search: Terraform: Reshaping the Data Engineering Experience Andre, an engineer at DoubleCloud responsible for its ELT transfer service, introduces Terraform for data engineers: infrastructure as code with providers, resources, plan/apply workflows, state, and reusable modules. The worked example provisions a data platform end to end — VPC peering between an AWS network and DoubleCloud, a ClickHouse cluster, and a PostgreSQL instance — showing how the same Terraform concepts apply across cloud providers.

nodes.label: Test, Containerize, and Deploy an AI-Assisted App
nodes.title: Test, Containerize, and Deploy an AI-Assisted App
nodes.search: Test, Containerize, and Deploy an AI Assisted App Third live coding session of AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp in which the system design interview app gets tests, Docker Compose packaging, and deployment to AWS via CloudFormation infrastructure as code, with a CI/CD pipeline set up for automatic deployment while the agent iterates on deployment failures.

nodes.label: The Agentic Shift in Data Engineering: From Pipeline Builders to Architects of Controlled Chaos
nodes.title: The Agentic Shift in Data Engineering: From Pipeline Builders to Architects of Controlled Chaos
nodes.search: The Agentic Shift in Data Engineering: From Pipeline Builders to Architects of Controlled Chaos Webinar by a 12 year data engineering veteran arguing that agents are becoming the primary data consumers, with machine identities already outnumbering human ones by more than 100 to 1. He covers on behalf of token access for agents, agent observability aligned with OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions and agent spans, and audit trails that record who acted on whose behalf.

nodes.label: The Importance of Data Quality
nodes.title: The Importance of Data Quality
nodes.search: The Importance of Data Quality YData's chief data officer argues that poor data quality remains a leading cause of failed AI projects, walking through Google's data cascades concept, data centric AI practices, and how data profiling and synthetic data help fix training data before modeling.

nodes.label: The Trade-off Between Simplicity And Optimality In Problem-solving
nodes.title: The Trade-off Between Simplicity And Optimality In Problem-solving
nodes.search: The Trade off Between Simplicity And Optimality In Problem solving Webinar on the trade off between simple and optimal designs in real world ML, using a ride dispatch example to show how hidden assumptions (ETA accuracy, what objective defines 'optimal') flip decisions, and weighing scalability, interpretability and observability, maintainability, and retraining cost when choosing algorithms.

nodes.label: The Unspoken Relationship - Product Managers and Data Scientists
nodes.title: The Unspoken Relationship - Product Managers and Data Scientists
nodes.search: The Unspoken Relationship Product Managers and Data Scientists An algorithm researcher at Healthy.io examines the working relationship between product managers and data scientists in cross functional squads, using a running example to show how open conversations about uncertainty, progress, and options lead to better product decisions for ML features.

nodes.label: The War of Gradient Boosted Trees
nodes.title: The War of Gradient Boosted Trees
nodes.search: The War of Gradient Boosted Trees Why gradient boosted trees still beat deep learning on tabular data: a walkthrough of tree ensembles, iterative boosting that converts weak models into one strong model, and the gradient optimization behind the trees.

nodes.label: Three Stages of Real-Time Data Monitoring
nodes.title: Three Stages of Real-Time Data Monitoring
nodes.search: Three Stages of Real Time Data Monitoring Workshop on implementing your own real time data validation and monitoring from scratch across three stages: reactive manual analysis when something breaks, proactive data quality checks embedded in data and ML pipelines, and real time end to end monitoring with alerts.

nodes.label: Tracking and personalizing AI agents with Snowplow and the Vercel AI SDK
nodes.title: Tracking and personalizing AI agents with Snowplow and the Vercel AI SDK
nodes.search: Tracking and personalizing AI agents with Snowplow and the Vercel AI SDK Snowplow workshop on tracking and personalizing AI agentic applications built with the Vercel AI SDK: server side node trackers capture agent steps, tool calls, token usage, and completions into the same event dataset as client side web events, and Snowplow Signals aggregates that behavioral history into context for personalizing agent responses, with events also forwardable to destinations like Kafka.

nodes.label: Unboxing Design Docs for Data Scientists
nodes.title: Unboxing Design Docs for Data Scientists
nodes.search: Unboxing Design Docs for Data Scientists A machine learning engineer on Google's Trust & Safety team unboxes design docs for data scientists: why they matter, how to structure one with sections like objective, research, milestones, and postlaunch review, and the types of design docs used at large companies.

nodes.label: Unlocking the Door to Your Kick-Start Data Engineering Career
nodes.title: Unlocking the Door to Your Kick-Start Data Engineering Career
nodes.search: Unlocking the Door to Your Kick Start Data Engineering Career A data engineer (formerly at Jimdo in Hamburg) shares a practical playbook for landing a first data engineering role in Germany: referral driven applications, interview stages including mock interviews and take home tests, framing pipelines by business impact, building end to end take home projects beyond the requested scope, and using analytics or Zoomcamp experience as a stepping stone into data engineering.

nodes.label: Use Claude Code Like a Pro
nodes.title: Use Claude Code Like a Pro
nodes.search: Use Claude Code Like a Pro Workshop, on 2026 08 31, with Bhavani Ravi.

nodes.label: Using GenAI to Create Horror Stories
nodes.title: Using GenAI to Create Horror Stories
nodes.search: Using GenAI to Create Horror Stories Alexey Grigorev presents his pet project, an automated pipeline that turns photos of everyday objects into AI generated horror stories published as a Russian language podcast. A GitHub Action picks an image from S3 and a Python script prompts OpenAI for the story, applies an editing pass for Russian grammar, generates a DALL E illustration and text to speech audio, and publishes via RSS to Spotify.

nodes.label: Vector Databases: Embeddings, Semantic Search, and Hybrid Retrieval
nodes.title: Vector Databases: Embeddings, Semantic Search, and Hybrid Retrieval
nodes.search: Vector Databases: Embeddings, Semantic Search, and Hybrid Retrieval LLM Zoomcamp module covering embeddings, vector search indexing with a vector database, and hybrid retrieval for the FAQ assistant, with live comparisons showing that plain text/keyword search remains surprisingly competitive on this dataset.

nodes.label: Vibe Coding: Build a Game with AI
nodes.title: Vibe Coding: Build a Game with AI
nodes.search: Vibe Coding: Build a Game with AI Alexey live builds a playable game in 90 minutes by directing Claude by voice ('vibe coding'), demonstrating a context first workflow where the game loop, art, and sound emerge from iterating with the AI. He also shows how he uses AI to learn new domains, from Rust game rendering to polygons, layers, and noise.

nodes.label: Why Your Search Relevance Project Will Fail
nodes.title: Why Your Search Relevance Project Will Fail
nodes.search: Why Your Search Relevance Project Will Fail Doug Turnbull, search engineer at Shopify and creator of the Elasticsearch learning to rank plugin, explains why search relevance projects fail and how to avoid failure, drawing on his AI powered search book and relevance tooling like Quepid and splainer.
